defs: A scary dream
A bad dream that wakes you up at night
A frightening dream you have while sleeping
exs: Carlos woke up from a nightmare.
Mom hugged me after my nightmare.
The nightmare was about a very tall monster.

defs: Moved back and forth through the air
Moved in a curve, like on a rope
Went in a wide arc
exs: Carlos swung on the rope over the creek.
The door swung open in the wind.
She swung the bat and hit the ball.

defs: Word meaning "if not"
Used to say something happens only if another thing does not
Except in the case that something happens
exs: We will go camping unless it rains.
You can't come in unless you take off your boots.
Mosh will not eat unless you call him.

defs: Put things on top of each other in a heap
Stacked up into a big heap
Gathered many things into a tall mound
exs: Carlos piled the logs by the fire.
Snow piled up outside the door.
She piled books on her desk.

defs: Wishing and wanting something to happen
Wanting something good to come true
Looking forward to a good thing
exs: Carlos was hoping for a snow day.
I am hoping Mom will bake cookies.
Mosh sat by the door, hoping for a walk.

defs: A thick mix of flour and eggs before baking
The runny dough you pour into a pan for cake
A soft mix you cook to make pancakes
exs: Carlos poured the batter into the pan.
The pancake batter was thick and sweet.
Mom licked the spoon covered in cake batter.

defs: A book with recipes for making food
A book that tells you how to cook meals
A kitchen book with pages of food instructions
exs: Mom found the banana bread page in her cookbook.
Carlos looked in the cookbook for a cake idea.
The cookbook has pictures of every dish.

defs: Liked better than all others
The one you like the most
Loved more than anything else of its kind
exs: Banana bread is my favorite food.
Blue is Carlos's favorite color of all.
What is your favorite game at recess?

defs: White powder made from wheat, used for baking
Ground-up grain you mix to make bread
A soft powder used in cakes and cookies
exs: Add two cups of flour to the bowl.
Flour got all over Carlos's nose.
Bread is made from flour, water, and yeast.

defs: To squash soft food into a paste
To crush food until it is smooth and soft
To press potatoes or fruit with a fork until soft
exs: Mash the bananas with a fork.
Dad will mash the potatoes for dinner.
Carlos had to mash the beans until smooth.

defs: A cup with lines showing how much it holds
A tool for getting the right amount of milk or flour
A kitchen cup marked with numbers
exs: Fill the measuring cup with milk.
Carlos used a measuring cup to scoop sugar.
Mom washed the measuring cup and put it away.

defs: Did what someone told you to do
Followed a rule or an order
Listened and did as you were asked
exs: Mosh obeyed and sat down at once.
The children obeyed the teacher and lined up.
Carlos obeyed the sign and stopped.

defs: To take the skin off a fruit
To pull off the outer layer of something
To remove the covering of a banana or orange
exs: Carlos will peel the bananas for the bread.
Please peel the orange for me.
Dad uses a knife to peel the apples.

defs: Instructions that tell how to make a food
A list of things and steps for cooking
A set of directions for baking a cake
exs: Mom followed the recipe for banana bread.
Grandma's recipe for soup is a family secret.
Carlos read the recipe before he started.

defs: To mix food by moving a spoon around
To move a spoon in circles in a bowl
To blend things in a pot with a spoon
exs: Stir the batter until it is smooth.
Carlos had to stir the soup so it would not burn.
Please stir your hot chocolate before you drink it.

defs: A sweet white powder put in food and drinks
What makes cookies and candy taste sweet
Sweet grains you stir into tea
exs: Add a cup of sugar to the bowl.
Too much sugar is bad for your teeth.
Carlos put sugar in his tea.

defs: To rub something to make it clean or dry
To clean a surface with a cloth
To remove dirt by rubbing
exs: Wipe the table with a wet cloth.
Carlos used a towel to wipe his hands.
Please wipe your feet before you come in.

defs: To put out a flame using your breath
To puff air on a fire until it stops burning
To make a birthday flame go dark with air from your mouth
exs: Make a wish and blow out the candles.
Carlos took a deep breath to blow out the flame.
Dad had to blow out the match.

defs: A stick of wax with a string that burns
A birthday cake decoration you light
Something that gives soft light when lit
exs: Carlos put a candle on the cake.
The candle melted slowly on the table.
Mom lit a candle when the power went out.

defs: Tasting very good
Yummy and wonderful to eat
Having a great flavor
exs: The banana bread was warm and delicious.
Mom made a delicious soup for dinner.
What a delicious smell from the kitchen!

defs: A reason you give to explain a mistake
What you say to explain why you did something wrong
A reason, true or not, for not doing something
exs: Carlos had no excuse for being late.
"The dog ate it" is a silly excuse.
She gave an excuse for missing practice.

defs: To stop something from happening
To keep a bad thing from taking place
To block something before it starts
exs: Wear a helmet to prevent head injuries.
Carlos used a lid to prevent the soup from spilling.
A fence can prevent Mosh from running away.

defs: A small pool of water on the ground
Water left on the road after rain
A little bit of spilled liquid on the floor
exs: Mosh splashed in a muddy puddle.
A puddle of water spread over the floor.
Carlos jumped over the puddle in his boots.

defs: Being protected from harm
Being free from danger
Rules that keep you from getting hurt
exs: Wear a helmet for your safety.
Fire safety is important at home.
Mom taught us water safety at the pool.

defs: Covered completely by lots of water
Soaked or flooded with too much liquid
Put out or lost under a flood of water
exs: The little flame drowned in the spilled water.
The flowers drowned in the heavy rain.
Carlos's cereal drowned in too much milk.

defs: Cleaned the floor with a wet tool on a stick
Washed the floor using a long-handled cleaner
Wiped up a spill from the floor
exs: Mom mopped the sticky kitchen floor.
Carlos mopped up the spilled water.
Dad mopped the muddy hallway after dinner.

defs: Set fire to something so it burns
Made a flame begin on something
Started a flame with a match
exs: Dad lit the candles on the cake.
She lit the campfire with a match.
Carlos lit the lamp when it got dark.

defs: Stopped burning or shining
Became dark because the flame or light ended
Left home to go somewhere
exs: The candles went out in the wind.
All the lights went out during the storm.
Carlos went out to play in the snow.

defs: Because something might happen
To be ready if something happens later
As a safe plan for what may come
exs: Take a coat in case it gets cold.
Carlos packed extra socks in case his feet got wet.
Keep a flashlight in case the lights go out.

defs: Made someone feel upset or annoyed by disturbing them
Troubled someone so they could not relax or focus
Kept bugging a person in a way they did not like
exs: The loud music bothered Carlos while he was reading.
Please do not talk to Dad now; he said he does not want to be bothered.
The buzzing fly bothered Mosh all afternoon.

defs: A close friend, often a boy or a pet pal
A pal you like to play with
A friendly word to call a close friend
exs: Mosh is Carlos's best buddy.
Come on, buddy, let's race to the park!
My buddy sits next to me at lunch.

defs: A hidden home where a wild animal lives
A cozy, quiet place where an animal sleeps
An animal's shelter in a cave or hole in the ground
exs: The fox ran back to its den.
Mosh made a warm den under the bed.
A bear sleeps in its den all winter.

defs: Shook or patted something soft to make it puffy
Made a pillow or feathers look light and full
Patted something until it became soft and round
exs: Mom fluffed the pillow before Carlos lay down.
The bird fluffed its feathers on the cold morning.
Laura fluffed her hair after taking off her hat.

defs: Moving a little because you are weak or afraid
Not steady and likely to wobble
Trembling instead of staying still
exs: Carlos felt shaky when he climbed the tall ladder.
The old table is shaky, so please be careful.
Her voice was shaky before the big show.

defs: Given too much, so you expect to get everything
Gone bad and not good to eat anymore
Treated so nicely that you become a little selfish
exs: Mosh is a spoiled pet and gets many treats.
Don't drink that milk; it is spoiled.
The spoiled child cried when he could not have a toy.

defs: A loving name you call a child you care about
A kind word a parent uses for a dear little one
A gentle name that shows love for someone
exs: Come here, sweetie, and give Mom a hug.
Grandma called me sweetie and gave me a cookie.
Good night, sweetie, sleep well.

defs: Very bad and not nice at all
Making you feel upset or sick
Really unpleasant, worse than just bad
exs: The medicine tasted awful.
We had an awful storm last night.
I feel awful because I broke my friend's toy.

defs: To say you are sure something will happen
To promise a prize that you will win or be right
To feel very sure about a guess
exs: I bet Mosh can catch the ball.
Carlos will bet his friend a cookie that it will rain.
I bet you are hungry after the long hike.

defs: Lying with the body bent into a small round shape
Resting in a cozy ball, like a sleepy cat
Tucked in tightly with knees close to the chest
exs: Mosh curled up on the soft rug.
Carlos curled up with a book on the sofa.
The kitten curled up in a warm box.

defs: A long strap used to lead a dog on a walk
A rope that keeps a pet close to you
A cord that you hold while walking your dog
exs: Carlos clipped the leash onto Mosh's collar.
Dogs must stay on a leash in the park.
Mosh pulled hard on the leash when he saw a squirrel.

defs: To touch something with your tongue
To pass the tongue over food or a face
What a dog does to show it likes you
exs: Mosh likes to lick Carlos's hand.
Please do not lick the spoon.
I love to lick an ice cream cone on a hot day.

defs: Wanting to eat food
Having an empty belly and needing a meal
Feeling a need for something to eat
exs: Carlos was hungry after the long game.
Mosh looked hungry, so Carlos filled his bowl.
I am hungry; let's make a sandwich.

defs: A person who takes care of sick people at school or a hospital
A helper who gives medicine and checks if you are well
The person at school who helps when you feel sick
exs: The nurse checked Carlos's forehead.
I went to the nurse because my head hurt.
The kind nurse gave him a bandage.

defs: The part of your body where food goes
Your belly, where you feel hungry or sick
The inside part that holds the food you eat
exs: Carlos had a pain in his stomach.
My stomach growled before lunch.
Don't swim right after a big meal, or your stomach may hurt.

defs: How hot or cold something is
A number that tells how warm your body is
A measure of heat, taken with a thermometer
exs: The nurse took Carlos's temperature.
The temperature outside is very low today.
Mom checked my temperature when I felt hot.

defs: Wanting to drink water
Needing something to drink
Having a dry mouth and wanting a drink
exs: After running, Carlos was very thirsty.
Mosh was thirsty and drank all the water.
I get thirsty on hot summer days.

defs: Healthy and not sick
In good health and feeling fine
Feeling good, with no sickness or pain
exs: Carlos did not feel well, so he stayed home.
I hope you get well soon.
Mosh is well again and ready to play.

defs: A bucket full of something
A round container filled up with water or sand
One bucket with something inside
exs: Carlos carried a pail of water to the garden.
She filled a pail of sand at the beach.
Dad brought a pail of apples from the farm.

defs: The part you hold to carry or open something
The part of a door or cup that you grab
The grip on a tool or bucket
exs: Carlos held the handle of the pail.
The cup handle broke, so I used two hands.
Turn the door handle to open it.

defs: Wonderful and very, very good
Amazing in a happy way
Great, better than just good
exs: What a marvelous day for a picnic!
Mom said the clean room looked marvelous.
The magic show was marvelous.

defs: Making water fly up in drops all around
Hitting water so it sprays out
Playing in water and making it jump about
exs: Mosh was splashing in the puddle.
The kids were splashing in the pool.
Stop splashing, or the floor will get wet!

defs: To put a soft food thinly across bread
To open out and cover a wide space
To make something go over a larger area
exs: Carlos will spread jam on his toast.
Mom spread a blanket on the grass.
Please spread the glue evenly on the paper.

defs: A white powder used in cooking and cleaning
A powder that makes cakes rise and fizz with vinegar
A white kitchen powder that bubbles in a science trick
exs: Mom added baking soda to the cake mix.
Carlos mixed baking soda and vinegar to make bubbles.
We cleaned the sink with baking soda.

defs: To act in a polite and good way
To follow the rules and be well mannered
To show good manners when others are around
exs: Please behave when we have visitors.
Mosh tries to behave at the dinner table.
Our class will behave well on the trip.

defs: A person who comes to visit your home
Someone you invite to eat or stay with you
A visitor who is welcomed by the host
exs: Our guest arrived just before dinner.
Carlos gave his guest the best seat.
Grandpa is a guest at our house this week.

defs: To ask someone to come to a party or event
To ask a friend to join you
To say, "Would you like to come?"
exs: Carlos wants to invite his friends to dinner.
I will invite my class to my birthday party.
Let's invite Grandma to the school show.

defs: Mistakes where things get confused with one another
Times when people get the wrong thing by accident
Little errors caused by getting things mixed in the wrong way
exs: There were two mix-ups at the party.
The mix-ups with the coats made everyone laugh.
Name tags help stop mix-ups.

defs: Very tiny pieces of something dry, like dust
A dry, soft material that is ground very fine
Something dry and fine that can be poured
exs: The white powder spilled on the table.
Mom put chocolate powder in the milk.
The baby powder smelled sweet.

defs: To tell someone about danger before it happens
To say "be careful" so no one gets hurt
To give notice that something bad may happen
exs: Carlos tried to warn his friend about the wet floor.
The sign will warn people about the deep water.
Dad did warn us that the soup was hot.

defs: Very nice and makes you happy
Pleasing and full of joy
Lovely in a way that brings a smile
exs: We had a delightful afternoon at the park.
The cake was delightful.
Her song was delightful to hear.

defs: A tall piece of furniture with drawers for clothes
A bedroom chest where you keep socks and shirts
Furniture with drawers that holds your clothes
exs: Carlos put his shirts in the dresser.
The lost sock was behind the dresser.
Mom's brush is on top of the dresser.

defs: Just right, with no difference at all
In a way that is perfectly correct
Without being even a little off
exs: This is exactly the coat I was looking for.
It is exactly noon now.
Carlos did exactly what the teacher said.

defs: To stop being angry at someone who did wrong
To say it is okay after a mistake
To let go of blame for a friend
exs: Please forgive me for being late.
Carlos will forgive Mosh for chewing his shoe.
I forgive you for breaking my pencil.

defs: Not here anymore; missing
Left and not able to be found
Away from a place
exs: The cookies are all gone.
When Carlos looked, his coat was gone.
Mom is gone, but she will be back soon.

defs: Something that is hard and needs a fix
A trouble that you have to solve
A difficult thing that makes you worry
exs: We have a problem; the door will not open.
Carlos solved the math problem.
The lost coats were a big problem.

defs: Making a deep, rough sound like a frog
Calling in a low, scratchy voice
What frogs do by the pond at night
exs: The frogs were croaking by the pond.
I heard croaking all night at the camp.
Something was croaking in the dark grass.

defs: To take a long walk in the hills or woods
To walk a long way outdoors for fun
To go on a trail on foot
exs: We will hike up the hill tomorrow.
Carlos likes to hike with his dad.
Wear good shoes when you hike.

defs: The number after ninety-nine
Ten times ten
A big number written as 100
exs: There are a hundred stars in the sky tonight.
Carlos counted one hundred steps.
A hundred children came to the camp.

defs: In a way that makes a lot of noise
With a big sound that is easy to hear
Not quietly at all
exs: Mosh barked loudly at the door.
The thunder rumbled loudly.
Please do not talk loudly in the library.

defs: Plants, animals, and everything outdoors not made by people
The trees, rivers, and wild places around us
The wild world of forests and mountains
exs: We love to walk in nature.
Carlos took a photo of nature at the lake.
Birds and trees are part of nature.

defs: To wave your hands to make an animal go away
To say "go away!" to a bug or bird
To chase away a small creature gently
exs: Carlos tried to shoo the bug away.
Please shoo the chickens out of the garden.
Mom will shoo the cat off the table.

defs: In a worried way, not feeling calm
Feeling nervous and not comfortable
With a little fear and restless feeling
exs: Carlos looked around uneasily in the dark.
Mosh sat uneasily by the tent.
She waited uneasily for her turn.

defs: To think about something and want to know
To ask yourself a question in your mind
To be curious about a thing
exs: I wonder what is in the box.
Carlos began to wonder where Mosh went.
Do you ever wonder how birds fly?

defs: Making you feel afraid
Frightening, like a spooky shadow in the dark
Something that gives you a fright
exs: The dark forest felt scary.
Carlos told a scary story at the campfire.
That mask is too scary for me.

defs: A living animal or strange being
Something alive, like a bug, bird, or beast
Any living thing that is not a plant
exs: A small creature ran under the tent.
Carlos saw a glowing creature in the lake.
The tiny creature hid under a leaf.

defs: To shine softly with light
To give off a gentle bright light
To shine like a firefly in the dark
exs: Fireflies glow in the dark.
The moon will glow over the lake.
Carlos's watch can glow at night.

defs: Grabbed something that was moving
Found and held on to something
Took hold of a ball or a fish
exs: Mosh caught the ball in his mouth.
Carlos caught a small fish in the stream.
Mom caught the glass before it fell.

defs: More easily surprised and nervous than before
Quicker to leap with fright at small sounds
Feeling more on edge than usual
exs: After the story, Carlos felt jumpier than before.
The dark made Mosh jumpier.
I am jumpier at night than during the day.

defs: To walk around with no plan
To wander freely over a wide place
To move from place to place without a goal
exs: Wild horses roam across the field.
Mosh likes to roam around the yard.
Cows roam on the green hills.

defs: A dark shape made when something blocks the light
The dark shape that follows you in the sun
A dim patch that appears behind an object
exs: Carlos saw his shadow on the wall.
A big shadow moved across the tent.
The tree made a long shadow.
